current.text: Toronto traded for Kawhi Leonard, and Brandon Ingram left in the deal.
Quickley is a projected starter for Toronto and part of the expected closing five with Barrett, Leonard and Barnes.
Kawhi Leonard's arrival is expected to cost Quickley usage and shots. He should still have the ball a lot. Without Kawhi he would rank a tier higher.
Sean expects the highest-volume three-point season of his career, with Quickley playing mostly off the ball.
His pull-up and transition three-point shooting needs to return to his career averages for him to hit his value.
When Kawhi misses games, Quickley should run more on-ball pick and roll.
His draft position varies a lot. Experts have seen him go anywhere from pick 73 to the 90s, and his ESPN ADP was 114.
Experts call him good value around pick 96 and early at 73. Lloyd thinks you can gain about 15 spots of value on him.
He is a tier 7 point guard: solid, with limited upside.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games, or 56 to 57 if Kawhi plays 75 games.
Toronto is not deep. After a solid top seven, the next players are Shead, Graves, Anderson, Elijah Martin and Trayce Jackson-Davis.

durable.text: He is not a classic point guard and not a perfect on-ball creator.
He blocks almost no shots, even for a guard.

note: Quickley is a threes and assists guard (z +1.3 and +1.4 vs the pool) with a below-average FG% (43.5%) and almost no blocks. That makes him a natural fit for punt BLK builds. Both sites rank him around 88 to 90, but they price him low (Yahoo value 8 USD, ESPN 3 USD, average costs under 3 USD). Our league paid 13 USD last season, so a bid of about 5 to 10 USD looks fair. Early in the season, check his shot volume next to Kawhi, whether his three-point attempts really go up, and whether his pull-up shooting recovers.
